thread:
kai: heads up — since the telemetry client swap in eu canary, charts in the console are spiking CPU and causing frame drops. seeing this on heatmaps and sparklines.

maya: oh no. any telemetry logs?

kai: perf-bot posted some traces. attaching the important bits: `https://perf.internal/runs/2026-03-20/536789`

perf-bot: Trace summary — increased main-thread parse by ~35%, kvcache miss ratio up 18%, bundle eval time +22%.

jordan: did the swap change how we import the telemetry bundle? could be a new eager import.

lina: it did — earlier we lazy-imported telemetry on route enter, the tweak moved an init into top-level to fix a race.

sam: that was the fix for lost events in slow routes. We thought the extra 30ms was acceptable.

maya: acceptable >only for networked pages<, but not if it forces parse of a 120kb vendor chunk on first paint.

kai: exact diff: added in src/console/entry.ts — `import {telemetryInit} from 'telemetry/client'` at top; before it was called inside router.on('routeReady')

jordan: can we revert to lazy-init but keep events buffer? maybe wrap init with `requestIdleCallback` fallback.

lina: requestIdleCallback isn't reliable on mobile. alternative: init stub that buffers calls then hydrates when real init runs. we already have a small shim pattern in shared/utils/bufferedInit.ts

sam: quick mitigation: gate the eager import behind a feature flag and roll back the build for EU canary. I can push a rollback in 10 if we want.

maya: also noticed kvcache miss ratio up — could be because the telemetry change changed module graph and bumped chunk ids, invalidating client's prefetched splitpoints.

kai: yes, stacktrace shows more HTTP 200s for chunk requests with bigger payloads. bundle hash changed and our client prefetch map didn't match canary.

jordan: that explains the double-download. two things: 1) restore old import to stop extra eval, 2) invalidate relative prefetch map gracefully so clients don't double-fetch (or fallback to existing chunk map).

lina: for (2) we could add a small version header to prefetch manifest and let the runtime accept a mismatched manifest for N minutes before forcing eviction. cheap and safe.

sam: rolling rollback to eu canary now. will annotate the deploy with revert tag and keep canary traffic at 20%.

perf-bot: Deploy started: canary-revert-telemetry-eager-2026-03-20 by sam.

maya: while that rolls, can someone open a lightweight PR to move init into our buffered shim and add telemetry-flag? i can review quickly.

kai: I'll open one in a minute. patch will: 1) replace top-level import with `const telemetry = createBufferedTelemetry()` 2) call `telemetry.hydrate()` on route-ready.

jordan: add a test ensuring telemetry calls before hydrate are buffered and replayed, and a performance test that asserts no main-thread parse regression.

lina: logging note: also add a metric for "telemetry-init-eval-time" so ops can detect regressions without perf tracing.

sam: rollback done. eu canary CPU normalized so far in traces. keeping canary at 10% for now.

maya: nice. once the PR is in we should coordinate a staged rollout that flips feature flag then removes old import. no rush.

kai: PR opened: `https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4821` — small, includes buffered shim + metrics.

jordan: LGTM, left a small comment about the replay order.

perf-bot: Trace follow-up in 15m scheduled.

lina: thanks all. follow-up action items: sam/ops keeps canary low; kai/maya ship buffered init; jordan adds perf test; i'll spec the manifest versioning header.

sam: noted. will post when we fully restore traffic. :thumbsup:
